title: H L A genes and drug hypersensitivity

segs.text: Section twenty one. Immune system variants, the H L A genes and drug hypersensitivity. She called this area probably the hottest area of pharmacogenomics, and the newest, not the oldest. Many biologicals now on the market have immunologically based side effects, some of them autoimmune, and these are hard to predict. As more biologicals reach the market, these effects become more common, and more variants will be identified.

H L A molecules are receptors on antigen presenting cells. She said, They are the receptor that will present the antigen to your T cell. That starts an immune response. A variant may change the antigen binding site of the H L A molecule. The molecule may then recognize peptides that are not true antigens and start an immune response against them. So H L A variants change immune recognition. They are not metabolism or transport variants and do not change how the drug is handled. Polymorphisms in H L A B, H L A D Q and H L A D R have been associated with many drug induced hypersensitivity reactions.

Katzung Table five four pairs variants with drugs. The two she will spend time on are both H L A B. H L A B star fifty seven zero one goes with abacavir induced skin toxicity, which she said can be fatal. H L A B star fifteen zero two goes with carbamazepine induced skin toxicity, also potentially fatal. Do not swap them. The table also lists H L A B star fifty eight zero one with allopurinol skin toxicity, and a D R B one haplotype with amoxicillin clavulanate liver injury. How common these variants are varies across populations and is not yet well defined.
